runtime.execution: Async environment steps, generated typed function tools, thread offload for sync actions and optional HTTP environment service.
runtime.service_boundary: Environment/tool supplier consumed by agent; supplied environments own task state, external services own remote execution.

summary: Typed action IDs, batch ordering, safe/unsafe concurrency and timing/error observations are useful execution primitives.

inspection.scope: Read exports, tool schema/serialization, exec dispatch/locks/timeouts/results, HTTP client and concurrency/timeout tests.
inspection.limits: Not every domain environment/tool selector inspected; timeout/cancellation does not validate termination of arbitrary sync thread work.

actions.lifecycle: Callback live in environment; serialization omits implementation.

actions.name: Environment.exec_tool_calls
actions.output: Call-ID-paired responses, typed/text/JSON content and time info

actions.name: EnvironmentClient.reset / step
actions.input: Task state/action and HTTP auth/timeout options
actions.lifecycle: Remote task service request; failures may be placeholder observations by opt-in.

evidence.claim: Typed tool metadata plus callable; concurrency_safe defaults true, callable excluded from ordinary serialized state.
Malformed JSON tool arguments become invalid tool name with empty arguments rather than trusted executable input.
Each batch creates reader-writer lock, invokes async function or sync function in thread, and optionally times out/catches errors.
Typed/JSON/text results paired to call ID with monotonic start/end; concurrent gather then input-order responses.
HTTP reset/step client forwards optional API key and timeout; caller can turn HTTP errors into placeholder observations.
Frame contains serializable full/subset state and metadata, optionally deepcopied; not guaranteed original IO corpus.
Counter-based batch test asserts unsafe action count 1 and some safe action overlap.

tests.focus: Safe/unsafe execution overlap within one batch.
tests.oracle: Unsafe result counter exactly 1 and at least one safe count >1; only one batch and cooperating sleep functions.
pytest.raises TimeoutError for SlowEnv actions; does not observe whether sync worker keeps changing external state afterward.

strengths: Action schema, call/result pairing and lifecycle timing are explicit.
Per-action concurrency safety declarations are stronger than blanket parallel JSON dispatch.
limits: Unsafe lock scope is one batch; concurrent calls into one environment need an owning policy.
Serialization excludes executable callable, and timeout is not universal work termination.
arconaut_questions: Which actions are concurrent-safe across whole workflow/turn, not merely one batch?
Can every timeout/interruption report whether its external effect is still running rather than just returning an error?
